solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prevent everyone going to the end of wood

indicators.note: the word for everyone is placed after the word for wood, at its end

parts.note: a forest is a large wood
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone stops a whole crowd from walking to the far edge of a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to the end of' is a placement signal, not a journey: the second word is set at the end of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in advance so that something cannot happen is a synonym of prevent.

clue.text: Celebrity, female wanting the last word getting cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A famous woman loses the argument, never getting the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' is not the final say in an argument here but the closing word of a prayer; 'getting cut short' loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity as a state of being widely known is a synonym of renown.

clue.text: Farmer managed to get companion, top lady

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means managed
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the top lady in the land

explanation.surface: A farmer succeeded in getting a lady of the highest rank as his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = the Queen (Elizabeth Regina) and CH = Companion of Honour are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs a large livestock farm, especially in America, is a kind of farmer.

clue.text: In street sits little old drunkard

indicators.note: in, with sits, says one piece is set inside the other
the short form of old sits within the street abbreviation

parts.note: little old means the abbreviation of old, O

explanation.surface: An old drunk sits about in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'sits' together put O inside ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual heavy drinker is called a sot, an old word for a soak.

clue.text: Woman dubbed "la Douce" hugged by an aviator

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside the arms of the other piece

parts.note: Irma la Douce is the heroine of the French musical and film of that name

explanation.surface: A sweet Frenchwoman is embraced by a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: Irma la Douce is a 1956 French stage musical, later a Billy Wilder film, about a Paris streetwalker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot or crew member of an aircraft, especially in an air force, is an aviator.

clue.text: Places you can read stories about Irish gathering support

indicators.note: the word for stories goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: lies are stories, as in telling stories

indicators.note: the Irish abbreviation gathers the garment for support within it

parts.note: a bra is a garment of support

explanation.surface: Tall tales about the Irish win backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' and 'about' nest one container in another: support sits in the Irish abbreviation, and that whole group sits in the stories word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Buildings holding books for the public to borrow or consult are places for reading.

clue.text: Vehicle almost completely destroyed

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, its last letter dropped

parts.note: bust means broken beyond repair, completely destroyed

explanation.surface: A vehicle has been nearly written off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger road vehicle running a regular route is a vehicle.

clue.text: Curry dish — the thing experimental unit served up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: it is the pronoun for the thing
a lab is a unit for experiments

explanation.surface: A curry is served by a test kitchen, which says it is just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns ITLAB backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a small wok-like pan, a Birmingham favourite.

clue.text: Conservative overwhelmed by shame messed up plan

indicators.note: the abbreviation is engulfed, swamped, by the jumbled letters around it
messed up means the letters of shame are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A Tory, swamped with disgrace, has botched a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' rearranges SHAME as SHEMA; 'overwhelmed by' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline or diagrammatic scheme is a synonym of a plan.

clue.text: Ogre featured in sermons — terrible!

indicators.note: featured in means the letters appear within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An ogre appears in sermons, and terrible ones at that.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'sermons' and the start of 'terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a frightening giant of folklore, a kind of fearsome creature.

clue.text: Sir Toby's expulsion after meal?

definitions.meaning: the surname of the drunken knight Sir Toby in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
a noisy release of wind from the stomach after eating

explanation.surface: What the knight lets out once dinner is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Toby is the boozy uncle of Olivia in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; his surname fits his nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A burp of air from the stomach is the classic noise made after a large meal.

clue.text: Dishonesty getting last chairman sacked

indicators.note: sacked, as in a city ransacked, signals the letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Fraud leads to the most recent company head being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges the letters of LAST CHAIRMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Quackery, pretending to skill one lacks, is a form of dishonesty.

clue.text: Presentation concerning period for imbibing drink

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the drink goes inside the other letters

parts.note: re means concerning, about
an age is a period of time
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A talk about a time set aside for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning period' is one unit that does the imbibing: the drink goes between its two parts, not around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of news, a journalistic presentation of events.

clue.text: Mouth silent monk only half needed

indicators.note: only half needed means just the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: Trappist monks are known for their vow of silence

explanation.surface: A monk vowed to silence needs only half a mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half needed' keeps the first four of TRAPPIST's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: Warriors making personal claim to holiness?

parts.note: I'm, short for I am, is a claim about oneself
pi is informal for pious, so the claim is to be holy

explanation.surface: Fighters assert that they are saintly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'I'm pi': I am pious. PI is a crossword-favourite slang word for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a regiment of Zulu warriors.

clue.text: Demonstration in favour of having international match

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A rally for a game between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test (match) is a match between national teams, chiefly in cricket and rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A public march or rally objecting to something is a demonstration.

clue.text: Showed discomfort in church when beset by gastric problem

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the church letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: wind is a gastric problem, flatulence
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A worshipper squirmed in the pew, suffering an attack of indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in church' looks like the setting of the scene; 'in' is just a link and church supplies its usual abbreviation for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or grimace in pain is a visible sign of discomfort.

clue.text: Hint given by superior gent, carrying minimal cash

indicators.note: carrying means the posh fellow holds the small sum within him

parts.note: a toff is an upper-class gentleman
1p, one penny, is minimal cash, with 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A posh man with hardly any money passes on a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a posh man; 1p is the British one-penny coin, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of advance inside information is a hint or warning.

clue.text: Break during academic period — is boy outside front of institute?

parts.note: in means during
a term is a period of the school or university year

indicators.note: the boy goes outside, around, the initial letter

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A student asks whether a boy outside the college is on a mid-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives I from institute; 'outside' puts SON around it, making SION.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval in a play or film is a break in the performance.

clue.text: One that grabs cards laid out on table

definitions.meaning: the claw of a bird of prey, which seizes its quarry
in card games, the stock of undealt cards left on the table

explanation.surface: A card sharp lays out a hand and snatches the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game sense, the stock left after dealing, is less known than the claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claw is the part that grips, and the term also names the undealt pack in card games.

clue.text: Try in this place to be listened to

indicators.note: listened to signals that the word is to be taken as spoken, by its sound

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to come here to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is a court's verb: a judge tries, or hears, a case. 'to be listened to' turns HERE into its sound-twin.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hearing a case is trying it, so the legal sense of try matches.

clue.text: Another girl upsetting Alice

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters of the name are disordered

explanation.surface: A second young woman is bothering Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Celia is a girl's name, a different one from the Alice in the clue.

clue.text: Detestable bit of play written by old boy

indicators.note: written by places the play's part next to the former pupil, after him

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a scene is a part of a play

explanation.surface: A former pupil has written a loathsome piece of drama.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is British for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offensively repugnant or disgusting is detestable.

clue.text: Knight in prison with time to waste

indicators.note: to waste means to throw away, so the time letter is discarded

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A knight who is in jail has time to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to waste' drops T from STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is addressed by this title before his first name.

clue.text: Boy in study retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Ned is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad backs away in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns NED backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a small private room for work or study.

clue.text: Author from abroad hiding in trees crazily

indicators.note: hiding in means the first jumble is concealed within the second
crazily signals the letters of trees put into a mad order
abroad means all over the place, so the letters of from are scattered

explanation.surface: A writer from overseas is lurking madly among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from abroad' looks like a foreign author, but 'abroad' scrambles the word from; 'crazily' scrambles trees into ESTER, and 'hiding in' puts the first jumble, MFOR, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist of A Passage to India and Howards End is an English author.
